model: Extra Trees Regressor (anchored on last season's yield)
evaluated_on: temporal holdout: train <2018, test 2018-2020, one season ahead
note: Reported metrics come from the holdout fit. The shipped .pkl is refit on all years for production use; it is never evaluated on data it has seen.

forecast_design.task: One-season-ahead yield for a state x crop x season series.
forecast_design.anchor: The model learns the change from last season's recorded yield (mean of the earlier seasons that exist when last season is missing).
forecast_design.requires: At least one recorded season in the three years before the forecast year.

series_mean.label: State x crop x season average over the training years

data_quality.exclusion_reason: Coconut is recorded in nuts/ha within a tonnes/ha column; winsorisation at the dataset cap collapsed most of its rows to a single value, which v2 memorised for a fake MAE of 0.000.

leakage.history_source: Every history feature, including yield_lag1, is recomputed per state x crop x season from strictly earlier calendar years (forecasting.add_history), not read from the CSV. test_model.py proves no lookahead.

data_quality.known_ceiling: Soil (N/P/K/pH) is a single constant per state and weather is state-year level, so every crop sharing a state-year has an identical input vector. Once a series' own history is known, these inputs add no measurable accuracy (see ablation). Closing this needs district-level soil/weather data, not a different algorithm.
